This time we headed to northern Moravia, to the Rychleby Mountains to be precise, where we supplied an existing family house with a BC 4 BASIC wastewater treatment plant.

Installation was complicated in this case, as the WWTP was being fitted into the first chamber of an existing concrete septic tank that was no longer fit for purpose. There was practically no room to manoeuvre, and connecting the WWTP to the sewer pipe was a real puzzle.

A so-called "pump shaft" was placed next to the BC 4 BASIC WWTP tank. It will house a submersible pump which, if the groundwater level rises, will pump water into a nearby stream. This system is a proven feature in, for example, locations close to watercourses.

02In this case the blower is housed in an underground plastic chamber.

In this case the blower is housed in an underground plastic chamber. The blower's operation is controlled by a time relay in the main electrical distribution board in the building.

The treated wastewater comfortably meets the parameters for discharge into surface water. In this case the outlet pipe runs into the bed of a small watercourse that flows right past the client's plot.
